method_notes: Weighted R32 performance and group stage form heavily, with secondary consideration for historical knockout pedigree and squad depth. Penalty shootout wins in R32 (Paraguay, Morocco, Egypt) noted as a mild fatigue and luck factor going into this round.

predictions.reasoning: France were the tournament's most dominant group-stage side and thrashed Sweden 3-0 in R32; Paraguay needed penalties to survive Germany and are significantly outclassed here.
Canada have been clinical and defensively solid; Morocco needed penalties to beat Netherlands and carry some fatigue, though their defensive organisation makes this close.
Brazil were the standout Group C side and beat Japan convincingly; Norway's goals came against weaker opposition and Brazil's quality across the pitch is a clear step up.
England topped Group L comfortably and have superior squad depth; Mexico won their group but their R32 win over Ecuador was functional rather than convincing.
Spain were imperious in the group stage and crushed Austria 3-0; Portugal scraped through as Group K runners-up and Spain's pressing system historically troubles them.
USA were solid throughout and beat Bosnia comfortably on home soil advantage; Belgium edged Senegal 3-2 showing defensive fragility that USA's pace can exploit.
Colombia topped Group K and have been defensively miserly; Egypt needed a penalty shootout to beat Australia and their open-play threat is limited.
Argentina were the only side with a perfect nine points and showed attacking variety; Switzerland are organised but Argentina's knockout pedigree and individual quality edges this.
